requirement_text.REQ-043: Add the priv/repo/migrations and Ecto.Schema modules the instance engine needs but that S2 deliberately did not build, all schema-per-tenant via REQ-022's :prefix mechanism (Decision B's general rule for business tables -- none of these three is GLOBAL, and none needs REQ-041's GLOBAL-exception flagging, since R-Co's own 005_instances.sql tables are per-tenant like events/events_archive): (a) an ALTER TABLE migration on REQ-023's instance_projections adding exactly the columns REQ-023's own migration header names as S3/EE-01's job: definition_id, correlation_key, current_nodes, variables, error_detail, completed_at, cancelled_at, plus uq_instance_correlation (partial unique) and idx_proj_definition. (b) a tasks table: id, instance_id, token_id, node_id, node_name, status (Ecto.Enum PENDING/COMPLETED/CANCELLED), assignee_type, assignee_ref, form_schema, output_variables, completed_by, completed_at/cancelled_at, timestamps(). The standalone task query/list surface (src/tasks/store.zig's own list/filter operations) is NOT ported here. (c) a tokens table: id, instance_id, node_id, branch_id, plus whatever the parallel token model needs -- resolved BUILD in the design (lib/letflow/design/req043-instance-engine-schema.md section 3.1). tenant_id on every table above is NOT NULL with no DB default and is derived internally, never a caller-supplied field, reusing Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1.

task.description: WF-02 Step 3 for REQ-043. Scope test already run by ORCH: YES, application-executable surface exists (new Ecto schema modules Letflow.Engine.Token/Letflow.Engine.Task, changesets, custom Ecto.Type, migrations) -- proceed with the full test-design procedure, do not skip to Step 5. ELIXIR-DEV already added/updated some fixture-level test changes as a mechanical consequence of its own implementation (test/letflow/event_store_test.exs's seed_projection!/4, test/letflow/event_store/schemas_test.exs's moduledoc-substring assertions) -- read those first so you don't duplicate coverage that already exists; your job is the acceptance-criteria-level coverage those fixture tweaks don't provide (uniqueness enforcement, tenant_id internal-derivation enforcement, enum restriction, array round-trip). Write test/specs/REQ-043.md plus test code under test/letflow/.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-043 acceptance criterion has at least one test case that would fail if violated
A test demonstrating uq_instance_correlation rejects a second instance_projections row with the same (definition_id, correlation_key) while permitting any number of NULL-correlation_key rows

A test demonstrating a row written into tasks (and tokens) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally; a test deliberately making a caller-supplied tenant_id disagree with the target schema fails loudly rather than silently attributing to the wrong tenant
A test confirming tasks.status Ecto.Enum accepts only PENDING/COMPLETED/CANCELLED
A test confirming current_nodes (via the new JSONArray custom Ecto.Type) round-trips a list through real Postgres without corruption
A test confirming all three new/altered migrations apply cleanly and are schema-per-tenant (no-op under no :prefix)
Test specs written before/alongside test code, not as an afterthought
No test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, self-sufficient, no cross-test pollution, no hardcoded secrets

result.summary: Scope test verdict re-confirmed YES (real Ecto.Schema modules, changesets, a custom Ecto.Type, and load-bearing migration conditionals -- not docs/build-config). Wrote test/specs/REQ-043.md plus three new test files: test/letflow/event_store/json_array_test.exs (pure unit tests for the JSONArray custom Ecto.Type's cast/1, load/1, dump/1), test/letflow/engine/schemas_test.exs (pure tests for Letflow.Engine.Token/Task -- table/prefix mapping, Ecto.Enum closed-set + casing for both tables, changeset required-field and immutability structure, and the design-mandated moduledoc content), and test/letflow/engine/migrations_test.exs (integration tests against real Postgres via Letflow.DataCase -- uq_instance_correlation partial-unique-index enforcement including the NULL-permitting case and the different-definition_id contrast case, current_nodes JSONArray round-trip through real Postgres for both a non-empty list and the schema-level [] default, tasks.status/tokens.status raw DB column casing, tenant_id internal-derivation for tasks/tokens, and a scoped §4 no-op-under-no-:prefix guard test for exactly REQ-043's three migrations). ELIXIR-DEV's own event_store_test.exs/event_store/schemas_test.exs fixture updates were read first and not duplicated. Did not stop at 'wrote the files': ran the actual toolchain myself (Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29/Mix 1.20.3, real Postgres 16 container letflow-postgres-1:5462) against every new file -- found and fixed three real bugs the tests themselves surfaced (two validate_required/2 tests that were vacuously passing because %Task{}/%Token{}'s own schema-level status default masked the required-field check; one changes.status KeyError against Ecto's own no-change-recorded-if-equal-to-default behavior) and one atom-length SystemLimitError from several describe+test name combinations that were too long (shortened them; full rationale for each test's existence stays in test/specs/REQ-043.md, not lost). Final verification: mix compile --warnings-as-errors exits 0; the three new files run 52/52 green; the FULL suite (including all pre-existing tests) runs 725/725 green (673 baseline + 52 new, zero regressions); mix format --check-formatted exits 0 after formatting the three new files.

issues.description: This run's own acceptance criterion 3 ('a test deliberately making a caller-supplied tenant_id disagree with the target schema fails loudly rather than silently attributing to the wrong tenant') is not literally satisfiable against REQ-043's own shipped artifacts: Letflow.Engine.Token/Task ship schema-only, with no context-module function carrying a public attrs parameter a caller could reach -- confirmed by direct read of both changesets and both migrations (tenant_id carries no FK, no check constraint, no changeset-level comparison against anything). The design doc's own §6 point 2 states this explicitly and defers enforcement to REQ-045/051/062. Writing a test asserting rejection today would assert something false about the actual code (a 'No Speculation' violation). Addressed as honestly as possible: three tests cover (a) the correct-derivation positive case, (b) storage-level tenant/schema isolation, and (c) an explicit, deliberately-tripwired pin of today's real behavior (a disagreeing tenant_id is currently ACCEPTED, not rejected) -- written to fail the moment enforcement is added without updating it. Recommend REQ-045's own TEST-DESIGNER add the literal 'rejects a disagreeing tenant_id' regression test once Letflow.Engine's real context-module function exists to reject it. This is an Instruction Precedence conflict between this run's handoff task.acceptance_criteria (likely copied from ELIXIR-DEV's own Step 2a criteria, which reused REQ-025's EventStore.append/2-shaped wording) and REQ-043's actual schema-only scope -- flagged per core-directives.md rather than silently resolved.
